info.name: Task 3 - Query Orders by User ID
info.description: GET /api/integration/getOrders?user_id=... Run task3-seed.sql on the local DB first, then run the folders in order (SEC03 must run after SEC02). Query values are written decoded; Postman URL-encodes them on send.

item.name: TC01 - Sample user - exact body from the spec

exec: pm.test("Top-level keys are exactly user_id and orders", () => pm.expect(Object.keys(j).sort()).to.eql(["orders", "user_id"]));
pm.test("orders is a non-empty array", () => { pm.expect(j.orders).to.be.an("array"); pm.expect(j.orders.length).to.be.above(0); });

pm.test("Each order has exactly order_timestamp, order_status, order_total (no id / created_at leaked)", () => j.orders.forEach(o => pm.expect(Object.keys(o).sort()).to.eql(["order_status", "order_timestamp", "order_total"])));
pm.test("order_total is a number, not a string", () => j.orders.forEach(o => pm.expect(o.order_total).to.be.a("number")));
pm.test("user_id echoes the requested value", () => pm.expect(j.user_id).to.eql("AES45678"));

pm.test("Body matches the spec example exactly", () => pm.expect(j).to.eql({ user_id: "AES45678", orders: [{ order_timestamp: "2021-02-12T23:02:00Z", order_status: "Confirmed", order_total: 1200 }] }));

request.description:
**Expected HTTP:** 200

**Why:** Seeded row 2021-02-12 23:02:00 / Confirmed / 1200.00 returns exactly the spec's example.

item.name: TC02 - User with 3 orders - all returned

pm.test("user_id echoes the requested value", () => pm.expect(j.user_id).to.eql("MULTI001"));
pm.test("Totals are 100, 250.75, 3000 (order not asserted - spec does not define it)", () => pm.expect(j.orders.map(o => o.order_total).sort((a, b) => a - b)).to.eql([100, 250.75, 3000]));
pm.test("Statuses are Confirmed x2, Cancelled x1", () => pm.expect(j.orders.map(o => o.order_status).sort()).to.eql(["Cancelled", "Confirmed", "Confirmed"]));

request.description:
**Expected HTTP:** 200

**Why:** Needs `orders` as an array with one entry per row, not just the first row.

item.name: TC07 - Unknown user - exact message from the spec

exec: pm.test("Status is 200 or 404 (spec gives the body, not the code)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));
pm.test("Body message is exactly No records found for user_id: AES99999", () => pm.expect(j.message).to.eql("No records found for user_id: AES99999"));
pm.test("Body has no orders or user_id key", () => { pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property("orders"); pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property("user_id"); });

request.description:
**Expected HTTP:** 200 or 404

**Why:** Spec gives the body only. The status code is open - see the questions list.

item.name: TC08 - Not-found message echoes ids with spaces / symbols

exec: pm.test("Status is 200 or 404 (spec gives the body, not the code)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));
pm.test("Body message is exactly No records found for user_id: ZZZ 999", () => pm.expect(j.message).to.eql("No records found for user_id: ZZZ 999"));
pm.test("Body has no orders or user_id key", () => { pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property("orders"); pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property("user_id"); });

request.description:
**Expected HTTP:** 200 or 404

**Why:** The message must show the id as sent, decoded (not `ZZZ%20999`).

item.name: TC09 - Partial id must not match (AES456)

exec: pm.test("Status is 200 or 404 (spec gives the body, not the code)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));
pm.test("Body message is exactly No records found for user_id: AES456", () => pm.expect(j.message).to.eql("No records found for user_id: AES456"));
pm.test("Body has no orders or user_id key", () => { pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property("orders"); pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property("user_id"); });

request.description:
**Expected HTTP:** 200 or 404

**Why:** Catches a `LIKE 'AES456%'` query. Exact match only.

exec: pm.test("Either found with the right orders or the not-found message", () => { const j = pm.response.json(); if (j.orders) { pm.expect(j.orders.length).to.eql(1); } else { pm.expect(j.message).to.eql("No records found for user_id: aes45678"); } });

request.description:

**Why:** Not in spec. MySQL's default collation is case-insensitive, so this probably FINDS the user. Decide whether that is acceptable, then tighten this test.
